rounds.text: Jakharia Fabric Ltd is fundamentally undervalued, trading at a P/E of 9.24x against a sector benchmark of 15.53x and an EV/EBITDA of 5.31x compared to the sector benchmark of 9.17x [E6, E11]. A discounted cash flow analysis estimates intrinsic value at Rs 112 per share against a market price of Rs 59.5, leaving a significant margin of safety of 46.7% [E43, E44]. Profitability metrics markedly outperform sector benchmarks, with an ROA of 10.7% versus 3.04%, an ROE of 12.88% versus 6.43%, and an ROCE of 15.31% versus 7.96% [E8, E9, E10]. Profit growth is robust and compounding, evidenced by a 52% compounded profit growth over 3 years and an operating margin expanding to 10% in Mar 2026 from -1% three years earlier [E20, E29]. Furthermore, the company demonstrates sound capital management by reducing its borrowings to Rs 5.40 Cr in Mar 2026 from Rs 8.01 Cr a year earlier, backed by stable promoter holdings of 67.39% [E39, E41]. Conceded: the company displays negative operating cash flow of Rs -1.76 Cr in Mar 2026 alongside a 10-year compounded sales growth of -2% [E14, E34].

Despite reported profits, Jakharia Fabric Ltd faces severe structural cash generation issues, highlighted by a negative cash conversion of -0.53x and negative operating cash flow of Rs -1.76 Cr alongside negative free cash flow of Rs -2.97 Cr in Mar 2026 [E33, E34, E35]. Long-term top-line contraction remains a persistent headquarter risk, demonstrated by a 10-year compounded sales growth of -2% and a 3-year compounded sales growth of -9% [E14, E16]. Balance sheet liquidity is precarious, with a current ratio of 0.88x in Mar 2025 indicating that current liabilities exceed current assets [E38]. Price momentum is deeply concerning as the stock trades below both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages [E48], accompanied by a historically brutal peak-to-trough drawdown of -84.8% and a negative Sharpe ratio of -0.14 [E51, E53]. Furthermore, the company offers a 0.00% dividend yield despite its reported profitability [E4, E59]. Conceded: the company has reduced debt to Rs 5.40 Cr [E39] and delivered robust short-term profit growth with a 52% compounded rate over 3 years [E20].

Conceded: operating cash flow was negative at Rs -1.76 Cr alongside negative free cash flow of Rs -2.97 Cr and a cash conversion of -0.53x in Mar 2026 [E33, E34, E35], and the 10-year and 3-year compounded sales growth are -2% and -9% respectively [E14, E16]. However, the current ratio of 0.88x dates back to Mar 2025 [E38], while more recent Mar 2026 data shows borrowings have actively dropped to Rs 5.40 Cr from Rs 8.01 Cr a year earlier, reflecting a conservatively financed debt-to-equity ratio of 0.21x [E37, E39]. Regarding momentum and historical drawdowns [E48, E51, E53], the rules-based screen explicitly scores the company at 68 out of 100 with a high-confidence buy rating, backed by a robust 12-month price return of 24.9% and a position sitting 90% of the way up its 52-week range [E46, E50, E62]. Conceded: the dividend yield is 0.00% [E4], but this capital is clearly being utilized to compound intrinsic value, as demonstrated by an impressive 52% compounded profit growth over 3 years and a discounted cash flow intrinsic value well above the market price, leaving a substantial 46.7% margin of safety [E20, E43, E44].

Conceded: borrowings dropped to Rs 5.40 Cr and debt-to-equity is a conservative 0.21x [E37, E39]. However, pointing to Mar 2026 debt reduction does not erase the fundamental solvency risk of a current ratio at 0.88x where current liabilities exceed current assets [E38]. Conceded: 3-year compounded profit growth reached 52% [E20], but this metric masks severe, ongoing top-line contraction including a 3-year sales decline of -9% and a 10-year sales decline of -2% [E14, E16]. Furthermore, screen data flags recent bearish catalysts including a year-over-year sales drop of -30% and decelerating earnings growth [E67, E68]. Finally, the claimed intrinsic value and margin of safety [E43, E44] completely ignore the catastrophic reality of negative operating cash flow of Rs -1.76 Cr and free cash flow of Rs -2.97 Cr in Mar 2026 [E34, E35], invalidating any thesis that undistributed capital is compounding real shareholder value.
